title: Release Preflight and Change Classification for Inference
author: Mariana Lopez
summary: A prescriptive change-classification and preflight checklist for inference-related releases (API, model, infra, and observability). Establishes gates, ownership, test signals, and rollback criteria to minimize production regressions while enabling safe velocity.
body:
Purpose
This document defines a standardized classification for changes that affect Redwood Inference serving (APIs, runtime kernels, model variants, routing policies, and infra) and a corresponding preflight checklist and gating rules. The goal is to reduce production regressions, shorten outage blast radius, and make rollout/rollback decisions predictable.

Scope
Applies to any change that will be deployed to: hosted inference control plane, serving runtime (kernels, scheduling), model catalog entries (version/quantization changes), routing policies (fallbacks, region routing), or API surface changes that can affect latency or correctness. It does not replace product design reviews for feature requirements.

Change classification
1) LEVEL 0 — Configuration tweak (low-risk)
- Examples: Logging verbosity, dashboard retention window, non-path impacting feature flags.
- Approval: Owner sign-off in PR; automated unit + lint tests.
- Deployment: Direct to main with standard CI; optional canary.

2) LEVEL 1 — Behavioral change (medium-risk)
- Examples: Default batching window change, autoscaling parameter tweak, telemetry sampling rate, non-breaking API header addition.
- Approval: Owner + infra/test reviewer.
- Tests: Integration tests, canary with synthetic traffic, perf smoke (99th latency and token cost).
- Deployment: Canary 5–10% for 24 hours; automated rollback on SLI degradation.

3) LEVEL 2 — Compatibility-impacting change (high-risk)
- Examples: Model parameter update (changes generation quality), API contract modification (schema optional->required), KV-cache semantics changes.
- Approval: Design review + product + SRE review.
- Tests: End-to-end evaluation against canonical prompt set, regression test suite, cost delta estimate, security review if data-path changes.
- Deployment: Progressive rollout (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with manual gate at each step and a 48-hour observation window.

4) LEVEL 3 — Safety/Regulatory or P0 risk (critical)
- Examples: Data residency changes, encryption/KMS swaps, rollback of major routing fallback behavior, change that can silently leak PII.
- Approval: Exec-level sign-off, legal/security consult, cross-team incident readiness.
- Tests: Audit logs verification, privacy review, full DR rehearsal.
- Deployment: Restricted maintenance window, 2-person release, immediate rollback playbook prepared.

Preflight checklist (cross-cutting, required fields)
Owners must include a completed preflight report attached to the PR or release ticket. Minimum items: 
- Change classification (Level 0–3) and rationale.
- List of owners and on-call contacts (primary, backup).
- Affected services and endpoints (service names, k8s deployment names, model ids).
- API compatibility statement (breaking/non-breaking, client impact).
- Test matrix results: unit, integration, perf-smoke, evals (pass/fail + links).
- Telemetry and SLI baselines: 50th/95th/99th latency, error rate, tokens/sec cost estimate.
- Observability additions required: dashboards, alert thresholds, tracing hooks, new metric names.
- Rollout plan: canary percentages, duration, automated/manual gates, rollback criteria.
- Backout steps and runbook link (must include commands and time estimate).
- Security and compliance impact assessment (PII, KMS, network).
- Feature-flag or routing config for rapid disable.

Automated gates and gating signals
The following signals must be wired into the deployment pipeline for Level 1+ changes: 
- Error rate anomaly: +3x baseline sustained during 5m window -> fail canary.
- Latency SLO breach: 99th percentile increases by >20% or absolute > target for 10m -> fail.
- Cost per token delta: >15% increase over expected at canary throughput -> alert and require sign-off.
- Quality regression (Level 2): automated evals on the canonical prompt set must not regress beyond configured thresholds (per-prompt ROUGE/embedding distance/LLM-quality metric).
- Trace sampling coverage: new endpoints must emit trace id and sampling rate >= 10% in canary.

Rollback criteria (minimal actionable conditions)
- Immediate rollback if: sustained error rate > 2x baseline for 10m, or customer-impacting 5xx spike affecting >1% of traffic, or manual escalations from on-call indicating severe functional regression.
- Conditional rollback: increase in latency SLO violations > threshold for 30m without remediation.
- Quality-triggered rollback: regression tests show meaningful decline on >5% of core prompt set, or automated user-sentiment signal crosses configured threshold.

Runbook snippets (examples)
- Quick rollback (hosted API routing revert):
  1) curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://console.redwood/api/v1/routing/revert -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","to":"stable"}'
  2) kubectl -n serving rollout undo deployment/serve-runtime --to-revision=<prev>
  3) run scripts/observability/check-rollout-health.sh --window 15m

- Drain-and-validate (stateful kernel change):
  1) Mark node pool as cordon: kubectl cordon <node>
  2) Start controlled drains and observe KV cache miss rate: metrics "serve.kv_cache_miss_rate"
  3) If miss rate > 10% for > 5m, abort and rollback.

Observability and dashboards
Required dashboards for any Level 1+ rollout:
- Per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), per-model token cost, error type breakdown (4xx/5xx), and request volume.
- Canary vs baseline comparison panel with percent-delta.
- Model-quality metric panels (automated eval pass rate, embedding drift heatmap).
- Incident trigger dashboard: rollup view showing anomalies across latency, errors, and customer SLOs.

SLO thresholds and cost guardrails (example table)
| Signal | Canary threshold | Production threshold | Action |
|--------|------------------|---------------------|--------|
| p99 latency | <= baseline * 1.2 | <= target | Fail canary / page SRE |
| Error rate (5xx) | <= baseline * 3 | <= baseline * 1.5 | Fail canary / alert |
| Tokens per request cost | <= +15% | <= +5% | Alert / sign-off |
| Model eval pass rate | >= 98% | >= 99% | Fail if regression |

(Represented here in text; release-ticket templates include a machine-parsable YAML table.)

Testing and evaluation requirements
- Every Level 2 change must run the canonical evaluation harness (applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness) with a deterministic seed and include a short report with metrics, counterexamples, and suggested mitigations.
- Integration tests must exercise real batching shapes (max token sequences, heavy concurrency) rather than synthetic single-request patterns. CI must surface token-cost estimates for the change.

Ownership and roles
- Change owner: responsible for preflight, rollout, and rollback.
- Release coordinator: orchestrates canary schedule and manual gates.
- SRE: owns alerting thresholds and executes rollback on SLO breach.
- Product/ML owner: signs off on quality evals for model-impacting changes.

Enforcement and compliance
- PR checks: the code review CI will validate the presence of a completed preflight fields file (preflight.yaml) for Level 1+; absence blocks merge.
- Post-release audit: all Level 2+ changes will be subject to a 7-day postmortem-lite where telemetry and incident logs are reviewed.
- Exceptions: temporary exceptions must be documented and approved by SRE lead and the VP of Engineering.

Adoption guidance 
- Start with enforcement for Level 2 and Level 3 changes in Q1 2026. Level 1 enforcement (automated gating) should be phased in after we deploy the canary telemetry pipes (expected Jan 2026).
- Templates and CI jobs: a release-ticket template and a preflight.yaml schema are provided in the team wiki. Use the provided GitHub Action to post canary metrics to the release ticket.

Decision and rationale
We chose a classification-focused approach to balance developer velocity with safety. The key trade-offs considered:
- Conservative gating reduces incidents but increases lead time for risky changes. To mitigate this, we emphasize automated evaluation and parallelizable preflight tasks.
- Cost sensitivity: we include token-cost estimates in the preflight because model updates can silently double cost.
- Human-in-the-loop: manual gates remain for Level 2+ to capture nuanced quality judgments that automated metrics may miss.

Appendices
A) Preflight ticket template fields (YAML-friendly):
- change_id, classification, owner, services, endpoints, model_ids, tests_run (list), metric_baselines (map), rollout_plan (structured list), rollback_steps (list), observability_links (list)

B) Example preflight excerpt
- change_id: INF-2026-117
- classification: Level 2
- owner: mariana.lopez@redwood.ai
- services: [serve-runtime, control-plane, router]
- endpoints: [/v1/generate]
- model_ids: [redwood/llama-small:v2-quant]
- tests_run: [unit, integration, canonical-eval]
- metric_baselines: {p99_latency_ms: 210, error_rate_pct: 0.2}
- rollout_plan: [{percent: 5, duration: 6h}, {percent: 25, duration: 24h}, {percent: 50, duration: 24h}]

C) Related artifacts
- preflight.yaml schema: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/preflight-schema
- example GitHub Action: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/canary-pipeline-action

D) Ownership and escalation contacts
- SRE on-call: sre-oncall@redwood.ai
- Release coordinator: releases@redwood.ai

Questions or feedback? Please @mention the author on the PR or file a note on the team wiki page.
